name: subscription-agents
description: Eleven coding-agent CLIs as sub-agents, on the subscriptions their own CLIs are logged in to. Only the scripted agent has been run against this harness; the commands for cursor, opencode, antigravity, gemini, devin, droid, omp and pi come from vendor docs, the ACP registry and secondary sources and are unverified.

agents.label: Claude Code

auth.hint: Log in once: run `claude` and type /login (or run `claude auth login`). The harness hides its own ANTHROPIC_API_KEY from the agent so the subscription is used; to bill per token on purpose, add env {"ANTHROPIC_API_KEY": "${ANTHROPIC_API_KEY}"} to this entry.

agents.install: Install Node.js (the adapter runs through npx) and the Claude Code CLI: npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code
agents.modelsNote: Aliases accepted by the Claude Code CLI's --model flag (the CLI's own names, not dated model ids); unverified here. Any other name can be typed.

agents.label: GitHub Copilot

auth.hint: Log in once: run `copilot` and type /login, or start the harness with COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN set to a fine-grained token that has the "Copilot Requests" permission. The harness has no non-interactive Copilot login check, so its login state shows as unknown.

agents.install: Install the GitHub Copilot CLI so that `copilot` is on PATH: npm install -g @github/copilot (needs Node.js 22 or newer and a Copilot plan)

accounts.unsupported: Octo has not yet confirmed how to keep a second GitHub Copilot sign-in apart. The Copilot CLI has its own account switch: run /user switch inside it.

agents.label: Grok

auth.hint: Log in once: run `grok login` (browser), or `grok login --device-auth` on a machine without a browser. An XAI_API_KEY in the harness environment is forwarded to Grok and switches it to per-token billing: unset it to stay on the subscription.

agents.install: Install the Grok CLI so that `grok` is on PATH: npm install -g @xai-official/grok (verified against Grok CLI 1.0.77). For scripts its documentation recommends `--no-auto-update` for `grok agent stdio`; it is not in this entry's args because its placement is unverified: add it to a copied manifest if wanted.

accounts.unsupported: Octo could not confirm where Grok keeps its sign-in, so a second one cannot be kept apart.

agents.label: Codex

auth.hint: Log in with the Codex CLI (codex login, or codex login --device-auth on a headless machine); with OCTO_CODEX_HOME set, log in with CODEX_HOME pointing at the same folder.

agents.install: Install the Codex CLI so that `codex` is on PATH: npm install -g @openai/codex (the ACP adapter @agentclientprotocol/codex-acp is fetched by npx and drives it; the entry is available only when `codex` is found)

auth.hint: Run cursor-agent login once (browser), or start the harness with CURSOR_API_KEY set. Some installs name the binary agent.

accounts.unsupported: Octo has not yet confirmed how to keep a second Cursor sign-in apart; on a Mac it lives in the system keychain.

auth.hint: Start opencode once and connect a model provider with /connect; models are named provider/model. Provider keys in the harness environment are not forwarded: set them in OpenCode's own config or add them to this entry's env.

accounts.unsupported: Octo has not yet confirmed how to keep a second OpenCode sign-in apart.

agents.label: Antigravity
agents.verifiedNote: Written from Google's agy acp documentation and the CLI changelog (1.5.0 to 1.5.9, read 2026-11-15); not run with Octo yet.
agents.startHint: agy acp needs Antigravity CLI 1.5.0 or newer. Update agy (run the installer again) and check `agy acp --help`.

auth.hint: Sign in once in a terminal: run `agy` and sign in with Google, or run `agy acp --login` (paste a code; works over SSH). agy acp reuses that saved sign-in. The harness hides GEMINI_API_KEY from agy so the subscription is used; to bill a Gemini API key per token on purpose, add env {"GEMINI_API_KEY": "${GEMINI_API_KEY}"} to a copy of this entry.

agents.install: Install the Antigravity CLI 1.5.0 or newer so that `agy` is on PATH (default folder ~/.local/bin): `curl -fsSL https://antigravity.google/cli/install.sh | bash` (macOS and Linux; run it again to update).

accounts.unsupported: Antigravity keeps one sign-in in the system keyring, shared by its app, its command line and its editor, so a second one cannot be kept apart.

agents.label: Gemini CLI (experimental)

accounts.note: Logins are kept as files in the account folder, not in the system keychain.

login.label: Google account (sign in inside gemini, then quit it)

auth.hint: Experimental. Run gemini once in a terminal and sign in with Google, then quit it. The login state shows as unknown because Gemini has no login check Octo can run. The harness hides GEMINI_API_KEY from gemini so the Google sign-in is used; to bill a Gemini API key per token on purpose, add env {"GEMINI_API_KEY": "${GEMINI_API_KEY}"} to a copy of this entry.

agents.install: Install the Gemini CLI so that `gemini` is on PATH (see the Gemini CLI's own documentation); the entry runs `gemini --acp`.

auth.hint: Run devin auth login (add --force-manual-token-flow over SSH), or set WINDSURF_API_KEY. List models with devin models list --format json.

accounts.note: Devin keeps all of its data in the account folder, not only the login.

auth.hint: Start the harness with FACTORY_API_KEY set (needed on headless machines); the browser device pairing of droid cannot be completed by the harness.

accounts.unsupported: Factory Droid signs in with an API key, and Octo does not store keys.

auth.hint: Run omp once and sign in (credentials in ~/.omp); omp models --json must list at least one model. Set OCTO_OMP_DIR to use a separate profile folder.
Needs pi on PATH. Run pi and /login (or set a provider API key in pi's own config) first. pi-acp is a third-party MVP adapter and offers only a terminal login.

accounts.unsupported: Octo has not looked into keeping a second sign-in of this CLI apart.
